subject: R shiny: Check if some download is available to the user

messages.author: 08054800fb509d6e
messages.subject: R shiny: Check if some download is available to the user
parts:
After a file is made available for download to the user on the ui side, is there a way to check if the download is available to the client on the server side? 

This is my server file:

library(shiny)
library(shinyjs)
library(shinyBS)

shinyServer(function(input, output) {

  observe({

    shinyjs::disable("download1")

    if(is.null(input$file1))
      return()

    # download data
    data <- mtcars
    output$download1 <- downloadHandler(
      filename = function() {
        paste("data-", Sys.Date(), ".csv", sep="")
      },
      content = function(file) {
        write.csv(data, file)
      }
    )

    shinyjs::enable("download1")

    # Check if download is there    <=========================== ISSUE
     if(!is.null(output$download1)){ # This is what doesn't work
       # Do something
     }

  })

})

Where I highlighted the issue towards the end of my server file is where I am trying to check if the download is there. Is this possible?

Also, this is my ui file:

# Define UI for application that draws a histogram
shinyUI(fluidPage(

    fileInput("file1", "Upload file1"),
    downloadButton("download1"),
    helpText("Download after something is done.")

))


I know that there is basically no need to check if the file is visible to the user in my case, but I am just trying to simulate this functionality. Thanks.

messages.author: ca443e6eaa0e78ed
messages.subject: Re: R shiny: Check if some download is available to the user
parts:
Oh, you were asking whether the *uploaded* file was there, and based on that, whether to enable/disable the *download* button? (I assume you're saying there's nothing to download if nothing's been uploaded?)

isFileThere <- reactive(is.null(input$file1))
observe({
  if (isFileThere()) {
    shinyjs::enable("download1")
  } else {
    shinyjs::disable("download1")
  }
})

shinyjs::disable is an operation that has a side effect, and therefore doesn't belong in a reactive(), but instead in an observe(). I talk about this in the videos about Effective Reactive Programming on this page (it's a couple of hours long but quite essential information if you're serious about writing Shiny apps).
